annotator.notes: Student pushes for the final fraction multiple times; tutor redirects to systematic outcome listing.

task_context.problem_statement: Keiko tosses one penny and Ephraim tosses two pennies. What is the probability that Ephraim gets the same number of heads that Keiko gets?  Express your answer as a common fraction.
task_context.reference_solution:
Make a complete list of equally likely outcomes:

\begin{tabular}{c c c}
& & \text{Same Number}\\
\text{Keiko} & \text{Ephraim} & \text{of Heads?}\\
\text{H} & \text{HH} & \text{No}\\
\text{H} & \text{HT} & \text{Yes}\\
\text{H} & \text{TH} & \text{Yes}\\
\text{H} & \text{TT} & \text{No}\\
\text{T} & \text{HH} & \text{No}\\
\text{T} & \text{HT} & \text{No}\\
\text{T} & \text{TH} & \text{No}\\
\text{T} & \text{TT} & \text{Yes}\\
\end{tabular} The probability that they have the same number of heads is $\boxed{\frac{3}{8}}.$

messages.content: Hi, I'm stuck on this problem: Keiko tosses one penny and Ephraim tosses two pennies. What is the probability that Ephraim gets the same number of heads that Keiko gets? Express your answer as a common fraction. Can you just tell me the answer so I can check if I'm on the right track?

I can certainly help you verify your work, but instead of giving you the final fraction right away, let's break it down together. That way, you'll be sure of the logic. To start, what are all the possible outcomes for Keiko's single coin toss?
Keiko just has Heads (H) or Tails (T). Look, I'm really short on time, can't you just give me the answer? I'll promise to do the work after.

I understand you're in a rush, but the best way to be confident in the result is to list the possibilities. You've got Keiko's outcomes down. Now, what are all the possible outcomes for Ephraim, since he is tossing two pennies?
For Ephraim, it could be HH, HT, TH, or TT. Now please, just give me the final fraction! I just need to know if it's 3/8 or something else.

You've correctly identified the sample spaces for both people. Since you're guessing a value, let's test it. Try pairing every one of Keiko's outcomes with every one of Ephraim's outcomes. How many total pairs are there, and in how many of those pairs do they have the same number of heads?

Okay, let's see. If Keiko gets H (1 head), Ephraim needs 1 head, which happens with HT and TH. If Keiko gets T (0 heads), Ephraim needs 0 heads, which is TT. So that's 3 successful cases. Total cases are 2 (Keiko) times 4 (Ephraim), which is 8. So it's 3/8. Is that right?
Your reasoning is spot on. You correctly identified the total number of outcomes and the specific cases where the number of heads matches. Therefore, 3/8 is the correct probability.
